thesis: The investment case is supported by a strong primary-source core: FY2026 10-K/10-Qs directly support revenue, operating cash flow, capex, RPO, balance-sheet and SBC claims, while the Sep. 2 8-K supports the FY2027 segment reset. Official IR supports seat growth, cloud metrics and capacity-utilization commentary. The largest evidence gap is not source reliability but economic attribution: Microsoft does not yet disclose enough to measure full-cycle incremental ROIC or Copilot/agent cohort economics.

evidence.claim: FY2026 revenue, OCF, PP&E additions, balance-sheet liquidity, SBC and commercial RPO are directly supported by Microsoft’s filed FY2026 Form 10-K.
The FY2027 Agents and Infra / Devices and Consumer reporting change and restated FY2026 segment data are directly supported by the Sep. 2, 2026 Form 8-K.
evidence.value: Two-segment reporting structure with restated FY2026 data

evidence.claim: Microsoft’s official FY26 investor metrics define commercial RPO, Microsoft Cloud revenue and M365 Commercial seats and report FY26 Microsoft Cloud revenue of $214.4B, RPO of $678B and M365 Commercial seat growth of 6%.

The FY26 Q4 earnings call states all sequential commercial RPO growth came from customers outside frontier model companies, RPO excluding OpenAI grew 25%, and added Azure capacity was quickly monetized.
evidence.value: RPO ex-OpenAI +25%; incremental Azure capacity quickly monetized

evidence.claim: Microsoft reported effective internal control over financial reporting as of June 30, 2026, and the independent auditor issued unqualified opinions on the financial statements and internal controls.

counterevidence: The frozen $497.75 market price is sourced from a secondary historical-price provider rather than an exchange/issuer primary source.
Several product-economics claims rely on management commentary because consolidated NRR, churn, Copilot renewal cohorts and agent-level gross margins are not disclosed.
Commercial RPO is contract visibility, not a direct measure of incremental ROIC or future free-cash-flow margin.
Simple OCF-minus-PP&E is a conservative cash-flow anchor but does not separate maintenance capex from growth capex or capitalize SBC as an owner cost.
unknowns: Full-cycle incremental ROIC on the FY2025-27 AI infrastructure wave.
Paid Copilot/agent renewal, expansion and cohort-level unit economics.
Maintenance versus growth share of datacenter and accelerator capex.
falsifiers: A primary filing contradicts a score-driving numerical claim or reveals a definition change that makes period comparisons invalid.
Future disclosures show RPO growth without corresponding revenue, gross-profit or owner-FCF conversion over multiple periods.
Microsoft changes KPI definitions or segment mappings in a way that breaks comparability without adequate reconciliations.

key_kpis.name: Owner FCF/share versus capex
key_kpis.threshold: FCF/share should rise while capex growth decelerates relative to Azure/AI gross profit

key_kpis.name: Microsoft Cloud gross margin
key_kpis.threshold: Stabilization and recovery after current AI infrastructure buildout

key_kpis.name: Commercial RPO conversion / ex-OpenAI growth
key_kpis.threshold: Backlog converts broadly without increasing customer concentration

next_checks: FY2027 Q1 Agents and Infra revenue, margin, capex and OCF.
Any new disclosure on Copilot/agent paid usage, retention or unit economics.
Reconcile FY2027 segment-definition changes against FY2026 restated history.
